name: WezTerm
summary: A Rust terminal emulator and multiplexer that connects PTY-backed execution domains to terminal parser/screen state, pane/tab/workspace topology, GPU windows, configurable input, and scriptable control surfaces.
scope: multiplexer panes, tabs, windows, and workspaces
keyboard, mouse, clipboard, scripting, and control boundaries

features.name: PTY domains and child-process lifecycle
features.description: WezTerm creates local or remote execution domains and attaches panes to PTY-backed child processes. For pane output the mux uses a blocking PTY reader thread, a socket pair feeding a parser thread, and action delivery to the mux thread. Configured parser buffers and terminal scrollback are distinct resource budgets; pane exit behavior determines whether an ended process leaves a visible pane.
benefits: Supports local, SSH, WSL, and other execution domains behind a common pane model
Makes child process state visible to mux and GUI layers
costs: Remote domains add transport, authentication, and failure modes
PTY, process, and domain resources require coordinated teardown

features.name: Terminal parser and screen state
features.description: The term library parses terminal output and maintains screen, cursor, keyboard, mouse, image, and capability state that panes expose to renderers and input handlers.
benefits: Centralizes terminal semantics for GUI and multiplexed panes
Supports terminal capability negotiation and rich protocol state
costs: Terminal compatibility state is broad and protocol-sensitive
Scrollback, images, and pane histories consume memory

features.name: Multiplexer pane/tab/workspace composition
features.description: The mux layer composes domains, windows, tabs, panes, workspaces, and clients. The default local domain lives with the GUI; separately configured Unix or SSH mux-server domains permit attachment independently of that GUI. Multiplexed SSH requires a compatible remote WezTerm daemon and differs from an ordinary SSH terminal connection.
benefits: Provides persistent multi-pane organization and remote/client attachment
Separates session topology from GUI presentation
costs: Topology and attachment state increase lifecycle and synchronization complexity
A mux server creates long-lived processes and resource ownership questions

features.name: GPU window rendering boundary
features.description: The GUI terminal window obtains renderable pane content and paints cells, glyphs, selections, and decorations through a GPU-backed presentation path.
benefits: Efficiently presents multiple panes and rich terminal content
Keeps GUI/window and mux state connected through renderable snapshots
costs: GPU/window backends and font shaping vary by platform
Large pane sets and high-rate output pressure rendering budgets

features.name: Keyboard, mouse, clipboard, and action events
features.description: WezTerm translates platform key and mouse events, clipboard interactions, and configured key assignments into pane input or mux actions, with pane focus and overlays affecting dispatch.
benefits: Unifies terminal input and mux actions through configurable bindings
Supports selection, clipboard, pane navigation, and command actions
costs: Focus, modal overlays, and key tables alter event routing
Clipboard and paste behavior cross a host-data boundary

features.name: CLI and domain control authority
features.description: WezTerm's CLI connects to a running GUI or mux server to list, split, move, spawn, and send input to panes. Unix-domain configuration documents secure socket-ownership checks and a skip_permissions_check override; SSH mux domains use SSH authentication to connect to a remote daemon. Control-endpoint access therefore grants session authority, while terminal configuration independently sets scrollback and protocol behavior.
benefits: Makes terminal automation and policy programmable
Allows control operations to target structured mux resources
costs: Control clients can affect running sessions and input
SSH domains and external command paths require explicit authority assumptions

mathematical_views.question: How does domain PTY output transition through terminal parsing into pane state and rendered GUI content?
assumptions: Terminal state is pane-local or pane-associated
GUI painting observes renderable state after scheduling

mathematical_views.question: How do domains, processes, panes, tabs, windows, workspaces, clients, and GUI windows compose or detach?
assumptions: Clients and GUI windows can observe or manipulate mux state
Persistence is a topology property, not proof of process survival

mathematical_views.question: Which CLI and remote-domain connections can reach which pane, process, input, and workspace resources?
assumptions: Configuration and domain policy select authority edges
The model does not prove deployment security
